newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INL says in talks to buy US stake in NZ Sky.
newsitem.headline: INL says in talks to buy US stake in NZ Sky.

text.p: Independent Newspapers Limited (INL), which is just under half-owned by Rupert Murdoch's New Corp, said on Tuesday it was in talks to buy U.S.-based HKP Partners' stake in New Zealand pay television company Sky Network Television.

HKP, backed by two U.S. telecommunications companies Bell Atlantic and Ameritech, which also have substantial stakes in Telecom New Zealand Limited, has a stake of about 51.1 percent in Sky, which is not related to Murdoch's 40 percent-owned European-based satellite network BSkyB.
Bell and Ameritech together hold just under half of Telecom, which is also in the pay television business through a growing cable operation.
In February this year INL said talks seeking the purchase of a stake of more than 80 percent in Sky Network TV had ended without result. They had been going since October last year.

While HKP is the biggest single shareholder in Sky, a number of other companies hold smaller stakes. State-owned Television New Zealand has a core shareholding of 16.4 percent which it was reported not to be interested in selling last time around.
Ten days ago The Herald newspaper reported that some of Sky's owners had been courting sharebrokers to test the water for a possible NZ$800 million share float.
The public issue was believed to be a fallback option after the first deal with INL went sour, the paper reported.
INL shares closed up 5.0 cents at NZ$7.80 on the New Zealand stock exchange on Tuesday in thin trade.
The announcement was made after the market had closed.
